newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian unions condemn rally violence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian unions condemn rally violence.

text.p: The Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) on Tuesday condemned the violent actions of what it called a small minority during an ACTU organised rally in Canberra on August 19 against proposed new labour laws.

"The success of the mobilisation of tens of thousands of people on that day was overshadowed by the actions of a small minority of protestors at the Canberra rally, who engaged in behaviour not condoned by the union movement," the ACTU said in a statement.
The rally of trade unionists outside the federal parliament was called to oppose the government's plan to free up the labour market and weaken the influence of trade unions on the economy.
The rally erupted into violence when some demonstrators stormed the building and clashed with police.
The ACTU said the violent actions of a small minority of protestors undermined the collective objectives of the union movement.
"The ACTU regrets what occurred, including injury to police and staff, but is not responsible for the actions of a small minority of the 30,000 participants at the Canberra rally," it said.
The ACTU said it would continue a campaign against the five-month-old Liberal-National government's industrial relations legislation.
